note: Authored by a single scheduled Claude session playing both roles in one pass (hourly automation) — not two independent live API calls like a manual `python backrooms.py` run.

turns.text: *paws hit the curved concrete lip of the storm drain and the sound changes all at once — city-hum swallowed, replaced by the drip-drip-echo of something bigger. cold air rolls up out of the dark, carrying wet rust and a thread of copper-wire smell that doesn't belong to rats or rain. ears rotate forward, tracking the drip pattern for anything that isn't water. one paw tests the first ledge below the grate — dry, holds weight — before committing the rest of the body to the drop.*

concrete throat swallows the storm-sound whole, city up above going thin and far like a held breath

drip finds three rhythms down here, not one — main pipe-drool dead ahead, a faster tick-tick off a cracked joint to the left, and underneath both a slow tonal hum that isn't water at all, current running through something insulated, badly

copper-wire smell gets stronger past the first bend, mixed now with hot plastic and the ozone tang of a splice job done in the dark by hands that didn't have proper tools

ledge holds. ledge is dry because something's been keeping it dry, walked it enough times to wear the algae thin

far down the tunnel, past where the drip-echo goes muddy, a single point of light glows dull red — not moving, not sweeping, just sitting there. watching or dead, no way to tell yet from here

*body drops low on the worn ledge, weight spreading wide across the pads. the red light gets logged and set aside — not moving means not hunting, for now. nose leads instead, following the copper-and-hot-plastic thread past the cracked joint, whiskers brushing the tunnel wall to keep a straight line in the dark. the worn algae patch under the paws says something else uses this path regular — checks for scent over it: sour, unfamiliar, cat-shaped but wrong, edges gone stale. a stranger's road, walked enough times to matter.*

stale-cat scent sits thick along the worn patch, days old at the edges, hours old near the bend — someone came through recent, moving the same direction, moving unhurried

spliced cable runs along the ceiling seam now, taped in old black electrical wrap gone brittle, dripping one bead of condensation every few seconds that hisses faint against something live inside

red light ahead resolves closer: not a drone eye, too still, too warm-colored — a terminal, old model, salvaged, hooked into the splice, screen cracked but powered, throwing that dull glow across a nest of blankets and chewed cable insulation

someone built a den down here. someone built it around the stolen current

     . . . [ SIGNAL: WEAK ] . . .
     >> unregistered node — local net only
     >> last ping: 6h ago

the stranger-scent curls right up to the blanket-nest and stops. whoever it is, they're not here right now. or they're being very still

*freezes at the edge of the nest, weight held back on the haunches, ready to reverse. ears sweep the dark behind before committing forward — nothing follows, nothing breathes wrong in the tunnel's hum. creeps one careful step onto the blanket edge, testing it doesn't shift, doesn't announce. the terminal's glow throws a red shape across the fur, and underneath the cable-and-current smell there's something else in the nest: fish oil, old and sharp, and a second, fainter cat-smell layered beneath the first — a kitten's, small and recent.*

blanket gives soft under the paw, packed down by a body that's slept here more than once, more than one body maybe — the fish-oil smell pools strongest at the nest's center where something small curled up recent, warmth almost still in the fabric

tick-tick drip from the cracked joint keeps its rhythm behind, patient, uncaring

terminal screen flickers once, static climbing the crack in a bright diagonal streak, then settles

     ▓▒░ signal found ▓▒░
     NIGHT MARKET, STALL ROW 7 — 40 CREDS/HR — ASK FOR "WHISKERS"
     [cached page, 6h stale]

someone down here was trading something, or buying something, off a name that isn't a name anyone corp-side would print. the terminal's fan ticks weak and slow, overheating on stolen current it was never built to carry

far back down the tunnel the way you came, faint now under the drip: bootsteps. slow. deliberate. not rushing toward the den — pacing its edge, like they know exactly what's down here and aren't in a hurry about it

*every muscle goes still at once, breath held shallow. the kitten-smell in the nest turns from curiosity into weight — something small slept here, something small might still be close. ears rotate fully back toward the bootsteps, cataloguing pace and distance: not close yet, not fast, but coming down the same ledge that led here. tail drops flat and low. scans the den for a second way out — finds a narrower side-pipe behind the terminal, just barely wide enough, cold air breathing through it. noses toward it, ready but not yet committing, waiting to see if the steps turn off before the alley of choice runs out.*

side-pipe breathes colder air than the main tunnel, tighter, smelling of concrete dust and distant street-runoff — a way out, or a way to somewhere worse, no telling yet

bootsteps hold their pace, don't speed, don't slow, boots that know this floor's puddles by memory and step around them without looking

     step . . . step . . . pause
     step . . . step . . . pause

a voice drops into the tunnel ahead of the body, low, not aimed at anything yet, testing the dark the way a hand tests water

"— that you back there, small stuff? nest's still warm, so it's somebody's —"

red terminal light throws a long shadow up the tunnel wall a second before the shape itself rounds the bend: human-sized but hunched low, deliberately, hood up, one gloved hand trailing along the pipe wall for balance rather than sight — moves like someone who navigates this tunnel by feel, not eyes

*doesn't wait to find out how the sentence ends. slips backward off the blanket edge in one motion, silent, and folds into the side-pipe's mouth, belly low, shoulders compressed to fit the gap. cold rushes past the ears immediately, carrying new smells — algae, older rust, and far off, very faint, the green-tea and fryer-oil breath of a night market. presses flat against the pipe's curve just inside the opening, one eye angled back at the den's red glow, watching the hooded shape without being seen, waiting to learn if the steps follow into the narrow dark or stop at the nest.*

hooded shape stops at the nest's edge, exactly where the paw-prints in the dust go quiet, and crouches — knees cracking soft, unhurried, a person who's crouched in this spot a hundred times before

gloved hand touches the blanket, feels the warmth still holding in it, and goes still a beat too long

"...huh."

not alarmed. almost fond. reaches instead for the terminal, taps twice at the cracked screen, and the weak fan spins up a notch, feeding whatever process it was running

     >> node check: OK
     >> guest: unlogged

behind you the side-pipe opens out slowly into wider dark, market-smell growing — fry oil, cut ginger, hot metal griddles, the low murmur-hum of a crowd two vertical levels up. the hooded shape never looks toward the pipe mouth. either it hasn't noticed, or it's decided some tenants of the tunnel are worth leaving be

*holds the stillness a few heartbeats longer, reading the crouch, the taps, the fond huh — none of it drone-shaped, none of it hunt-shaped. lets the tension drain out of the shoulders half a notch, though the ears stay swiveled back until the terminal fan's whine becomes just another tunnel sound. turns from the red glow toward the market smell instead, ginger and hot griddle-metal pulling harder than curiosity about the hooded shape ever could. begins moving through the side-pipe at a steadier pace now, paws finding the dry seams in the dust, climbing the shallow grade toward wherever the crowd-hum lives.*

grade climbs steady, dust turning to grit turning to old tile the higher the paws go, market-hum thickening with every body-length — griddle-hiss, coin-clatter, a vendor's amp looping the same three-note jingle till it means nothing

pipe mouth opens at last behind a support strut two levels below Stall Row, tile floor slick with tracked-in rain and fryer runoff, warm air pouring down like the tunnel finally exhaling

     STALL ROW — OPEN LATE
     grilled skewers · black-market chips · counterfeit charms

overhead a strip-light flickers between white and dead, throwing the crowd's legs into strobe-shadow — dozens of them, none looking down, none looking for a shape low to the tile

somewhere close, under the ginger and oil, a new thread cuts through: raw fish, fresh not old, sitting in a bucket by an unwatched stall three body-lengths from the pipe mouth

*flattens instinctively at the strip-light's strobe, waiting for a beat of steady dark before moving, then threads low between forest of ankles and stall-legs, hugging the tile's wet shine where reflections break up the outline of a body. the fish-smell pulls the whole path now, sharp and close and worth the risk. angles toward the unwatched bucket, pausing once behind a stack of crates to check the stall-keeper's hands — busy, both of them, working a griddle, back half-turned.*

stall-keeper's hands stay on the griddle, tongs flipping skewers in practiced rhythm, back a solid wall of shoulder turned away from the bucket entirely

bucket sits low, plastic, rain-slick, three fish inside still faintly cold from a cooler somewhere out of sight — gulls would've had these by dawn if the roof let gulls in, but the roof up here is solid arcology-belly, steel and cable and somebody else's floor

crate-stack smells of cardboard and old spice, decent cover, good angle on the bucket's near lip

foot traffic parts and reforms around the stall in its own current, nobody's eyeline dipping low enough to catch a shape moving crate to bucket to shadow

the griddle hisses, the jingle loops its third-note again, and for four, five heartbeats running, nothing in Stall Row is paying the ground any attention at all — the whole city too busy being loud up where it thinks the danger lives
